scenario.title: Escape from Egypt
intro.text:
ESCAPE FROM EGYPT - 8 MAY 1943

Military Prison Al-Qabbari, Alexandria

The renowned hero now only a public enemy! Jailed in the military prison of Al-Qabbari you are waiting for your trial because of communist propaganda and insubordination against the Middle East High Command and the Greek government in exile. However, your friends managed to organize your escape to Greece and to provide you with a getaway car. At the airport of Alexandria a plane is ready for take off and alternatively a vessel waiting for you located in the port of Al Muaddiyah. Reach one of these points without to be caught at the control points of the Brits! Friends on the Greek freighters SS Dimitrios Inglessis and SS Thrace monitor the airport and the port for you!

GOAL Retreat your MSU via Exit Point!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-12-0-briliant.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.reaction-12-0-briliant.text: Ruweisat and Deir el Mreir fell before the Axis line could adjust to the main offensive. The Greek contingent has earned the dangerous privilege of being useful to every political plan for liberation.
line.reaction-12-1-victory-tactical.text: The assigned objectives were taken and the Axis position is withdrawing. The formation has proved it can fight again; now every claimant to Greece asks whom that force obeys.
line.callback-0.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.callback-0.text: You kept the formation under government command when leaving might have felt cleaner. I defended that as duty. The wire around these Greek barracks is where the defence becomes difficult.
line.callback-1.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.callback-1.text: Cairo's orders now call us deserters. The fishing captain is ready for the road home. Hale's sentries, unfortunately, are ready as well.
line.callback-2.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.callback-2.text: The Crete carriers remained together and became the formation's unofficial proof that retreat could still preserve skill.
line.callback-3.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.callback-3.text: The Crete transport pool vanished into the core. Its veterans are everywhere and therefore receive credit nowhere.
line.scene-0.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.scene-0.text: The captain leaves Al Muaddiyah when the harbour patrol changes. He has space for men or crates. Every officer who heard that sentence decided his own crate was indispensable.
line.scene-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.scene-1.text: I can provide movement papers for the first lorry and perhaps the second. After that, the guards will see an armed column moving without orders.
line.scene-2.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-2.text: Most of those guards are Greeks. Yesterday they shared our cookhouse. Tonight one of them may be expected to stop us for the sake of a government we have just left.
line.decision.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.decision.text: Do we take the transport and weapons we will need in Greece, or leave them behind and reach the boat without making this a battle against our old barracks?
line.decision.choice.take-the-arms.text: Seize transport and weapons before breaking for the exits.
line.decision.choice.take-the-arms.hint: Spend 50 prestige, give infantry and anti-tank formations 15 experience, and fully rearm the core.
line.decision.choice.leave-without-blood: Travel light and avoid fire on Greek or British guards unless the exit is closed.
Gain 50 prestige, restore the core to at least nine strength, and fully refuel it.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.choice-a-0.text: If a sentry blocks a crate, the crate stays. Force is for the road and only the road. I will not begin our return to Greece by inventing an enemy here.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-a-1.text: Store parties first, drivers ready, no firing without your order. We will arrive better armed and with more men wondering whether we stole from them.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-b-0.text: Light, then. The men will complain until they realise they can walk past a checkpoint without looking like an invading army.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.choice-b-1.text: Hospital stores, personal weapons, papers. Everything else remains on the inventory. Discipline must carry what the lorries do not.
